draft.title: Severity matrix for design findings
draft.principle_summary: Nielsen's severity-rating method scores a usability problem 0 (not a problem) to 4 (catastrophe) as a judgment call built from three named dimensions: frequency (how many users/instances hit it), impact (how hard it is to work around), and persistence (one-time vs recurring), with a noted market-impact modifier for perception-disproportionate problems. The common formalization averages three 0-4 sub-ratings into the final 0-4 score. A second, independent finding from the same research line: a single evaluator catches only about 35% of real problems in a heuristic walk, which is why any high-severity list needs a second independent pass before being treated as final. D10 needs both pieces translated from "usability bug" language into "design-drift finding" language (gate breach vs mechanized D1-D9 output vs unnamed subjective complaint), which is the gap this stream closes.

sources.claim: Nielsen's severity scale is 0 = not a problem, 1 = cosmetic, 2 = minor, 3 = major, 4 = catastrophe, computed from frequency x impact x persistence plus a market-impact factor
sources.source: Nielsen Norman Group, How to Rate the Severity of Usability Problems, https://www.nngroup.com/articles/how-to-rate-the-severity-of-usability-problems/

sources.claim: A single evaluator in a heuristic evaluation finds only about 35% of the usability problems present, averaged across six projects; returns diminish after roughly 5 evaluators
sources.source: Nielsen Norman Group, heuristic evaluation theory page, https://www.nngroup.com/articles/how-to-conduct-a-heuristic-evaluation/theory-heuristic-evaluations/

draft.solen_current: _design-system/RATIONALE.md section 28 "Gap register", the diagnostic-gaps table (lines 836-848). D10 (line 848) currently reads only: "Severity matrix: contract breach (gate-enforced literal) = blocking regardless of visual size; within-budget taste = cosmetic" with mechanizable marked "Skill edit", i.e. it states the two-bucket OUTCOME but has no rubric that produces it. The source material for the underlying scale already lives one layer down and is NOT yet cross-referenced from D10: _design-system/research/TASTE_DIAGNOSIS_FRAMEWORKS.md line 22 (the 0-4 scale + frequency/impact/persistence definition, T1), line 20 (the 35% single-evaluator stat, T1), line 56 ("rate each 0-4 for severity... before touching code"), and line 58 (the second-pass rule derived from the 35% stat). D1-D9 (lines 839-847) are the mechanized finding-producers this matrix is meant to consume, each YES/Gate/Procedure tagged but none of them emit a severity number today.
draft.gap: D10 is a bare two-bucket assertion (breach = blocking, taste = cosmetic), not a rubric. Three concrete holes: (1) no formula converting a D1-D9 finding's raw output (a pixel offset, a percent, an instance count) into the 0-4 frequency/impact/persistence sub-scores Nielsen's method requires, so "severity" cannot actually be computed, only guessed; (2) no explicit rule for where a LOCKFILE/frozen-literal contract breach sits on the SAME 0-4 scale as a mechanized taste finding, i.e. D10's own two-bucket split (breach vs taste) is not yet reconciled with the underlying 0-4 method it is supposed to be adapting; (3) no cross-reference to the 35% single-evaluator stat as an operational rule (a severity>=3 finding needs a second independent pass, e.g. re-run the diagnosis skill after a break, or a second reviewer/subagent, before it is called final), even though TASTE_DIAGNOSIS_FRAMEWORKS.md line 58 already states this rule in the usability-bug context and D10 sits right next to it in the gap register without inheriting it.
draft.proposed_addition:
COMPUTABLE METRIC: Design-Finding Severity Score (D10)

INPUTS per finding (one row per item on a punch list, whether hand-observed or emitted by D1/D2/D3/D6/D7/D8/D9):
- source_type: one of {gate_breach, mechanized, subjective}. gate_breach = the finding IS a LOCKFILE/SOURCE frozen-literal or hook-enforced-token violation (e.g. no-black-selected, a hex outside the token set, a retired token in use). mechanized = a D1-D9 script emitted it with a numeric measurement. subjective = an owner "looks off" complaint not yet run through the diagnosis skill's named-axis walk.
- instance_count: integer, number of distinct rendered elements/screens where the finding appears (count from the D-script output or from a manual sweep).
- component_reach: enum {single_instance, one_component_type, cross_screen_flow, global_chrome_or_token}. Whether the finding is confined to one element, repeats within one component across a screen, recurs across a funnel (2+ screens in one flow, e.g. the booking steps), or is a global token/chrome issue that touches every screen.
- deviation_magnitude: the finding's own D-script number normalized against its stated threshold, expressed as (measured - threshold) / threshold for continuous metrics (D1 centroid offset, D2 blue-coverage %, D3 px off-grid, D6 px under 44, D8 gap px off the 32/12/16 whitelist), or a boolean 1/0 for pass/fail metrics (D7 cross-surface diff, D9 locale overflow).

SUB-SCORES (each rated 0-4, following Nielsen's three named dimensions):

FREQUENCY (from instance_count):
0 = not present this pass. 1 = 1 instance. 2 = 2-3 instances, or one repeated component type. 3 = 4+ instances, or a component used on 2+ distinct screens. 4 = every instance of a component sitewide.

IMPACT: forced to 4 whenever source_type = gate_breach (a contract breach is maximal impact by definition, independent of how visually small it looks; this is the mechanization of D10's existing "blocking regardless of visual size" line). Otherwise, from deviation_magnitude: 0 = 0 (no measurable deviation). 1 = up to 25% over threshold, or a subjective complaint not yet named to a diagnosis-skill axis. 2 = 25-75% over threshold. 3 = 75-150% over threshold, or a named-axis violation with no existing gate. 4 = over 150% of threshold, a WCAG contrast/tap-target failure, or the finding blocks a user from completing the task.

PERSISTENCE (from component_reach): 0 = transient (a loading-state flash, not present at rest). 1 = single_instance. 2 = one_component_type, seen every time that screen is visited. 3 = cross_screen_flow. 4 = global_chrome_or_token.

SEVERITY = round(mean(FREQUENCY, IMPACT, PERSISTENCE)), clamped to 0-4.

TRIAGE THRESHOLDS (what the score flags):
- Severity 4, OR source_type = gate_breach (which forces IMPACT=4, so it can only land at 4 or 3 depending on frequency/persistence, but treat ANY gate_breach as an automatic BLOCKING regardless of the rounded mean, since a contract breach is not negotiable by volume): BLOCKING. Ship gate fails; cannot be marked "ready for review" (rule 7) until fixed.
- Severity 3: HIGH. Must be fixed before the CURRENT verifier-loop round closes (rule 9); does not block unrelated in-flight work.
- Severity 2: MINOR. Goes into _design-system/SUGGESTIONS.md as a parked item (per the design-suggest skill's queue), batched into the next design pass, not fixed inline.
- Severity 0-1: COSMETIC. Fixed only opportunistically (e.g. touched incidentally while editing the same file); never blocks or gets its own task.

SECOND-PASS RULE (T1, from the 35% single-evaluator stat, TASTE_DIAGNOSIS_FRAMEWORKS.md line 20/58): any finding scored Severity 3 or 4 must get one independent second pass (a fresh diagnosis-skill run after a break, or a separate reviewer/subagent per rule 9's verifier-loop) before the punch list is treated as final and used to gate "ready for review." Severity 0-2 findings do not require this, since their cost of a missed instance is low.

WHAT THIS FLAGS THAT D10's CURRENT TEXT DOES NOT: it gives D1-D9's raw numeric outputs (a percent, a px offset, an instance count) a deterministic path to a triage bucket instead of leaving "how bad is this" to eyeballing after the number is computed, and it makes explicit that a contract breach is not merely "high severity" but categorically BLOCKING, the two are on the same 0-4 scale but the breach path bypasses the mean and forces the floor.
numbers_used: 35% problems found by a single evaluator

draft.taste_lab_probe: Not required for a mechanize-tag stream (no new perceptual default is being proposed). Calibration path instead: backtest the formula against 5-10 already-closed punch-list items from past verifier-loop rounds (rule 9 history) where the owner's actual triage call (fixed-now vs parked vs ignored) is known, and check the formula's bucket matches the owner's real decision at least 8/10 times before treating the thresholds as load-bearing; adjust the deviation_magnitude band boundaries (25/75/150%) if it does not.

verified.title: Severity matrix for design findings

claim_verdicts.claim: Nielsen's severity scale is 0=not a problem, 1=cosmetic, 2=minor, 3=major, 4=catastrophe, computed from frequency x impact x persistence plus a market-impact factor
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed against nngroup.com/articles/how-to-rate-the-severity-of-usability-problems/ directly: the 0-4 labels match verbatim (0=not agree it's a problem, 1=cosmetic fix if time allows, 2=minor low priority, 3=major high priority, 4=catastrophe imperative before release), and the article does name market impact as a distinct factor. One nuance: NN/g does not publish an exact 'x' multiplication formula or a mean-of-three formula, it says severity combines frequency/impact/persistence/market-impact into a single overall judgment call without a stated arithmetic. The draft's own text already flags this correctly as 'the common formalization averages three 0-4 sub-ratings', i.e. it discloses this is an adaptation, not a verbatim Nielsen formula. That disclosure must stay in the final text.

claim_verdicts.claim: A single evaluator in a heuristic evaluation finds only about 35% of the usability problems present, averaged across six projects; returns diminish after roughly 5 evaluators
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed against nngroup.com/articles/how-to-conduct-a-heuristic-evaluation/theory-heuristic-evaluations/: 'single evaluators found only 35 percent of the usability problems in the interfaces, averaged over six... projects' is Nielsen's own stated figure. Nielsen's actual recommendation is 3-5 evaluators uncover ~75% of issues, with returns flattening past that range, close enough to 'diminishing returns after ~5' to hold as T1, though the draft's phrasing slightly compresses the nuance (Nielsen frames it as 3-5 being the sweet spot, not literally 'after 5 it drops off a cliff').

claim_verdicts.claim: 35% problems found by a single evaluator (numbers_used)
claim_verdicts.note: Verified verbatim as above; not on the never-cite myth screen (checked _plans/TASTE_R3_STREAMS.json myth_screen field, which lists 2000%-sample-lift, 70-90%-defaults, 2x-loss-aversion, jam-study, $300M-button, 5%-retention-25-95%-profit, 5-25x-cheaper-retention, Amazon-100ms, Duolingo-+20%, UGC-4x; the 35%-single-evaluator stat is a different, independently-sourced NN/g figure and is not among the banned numbers).
Matches Nielsen's stated 3-5 evaluator recommendation; T1 held but softened wording recommended (see residual_risks).

claim_verdicts.tier_final: T3 (self-derived, not sourced from Nielsen or any external study)
claim_verdicts.note: These are NOT in the NN/g source material anywhere, they are new numeric thresholds invented for this stream to operationalize the IMPACT sub-score. The draft is honest about this in its own taste_lab_probe (calls for backtesting against 5-10 closed punch-list items before treating them as load-bearing), so this is disclosed, not smuggled in as T1. Tier must read T3/unverified-heuristic in the RATIONALE entry, not silently inherit the T1 tier of the surrounding Nielsen material.
Confirmed as an existing Solen-internal locked constant referenced elsewhere in the codebase's own design system docs, not an external stat, correctly labeled as already-locked in the draft.
Matches the project's own locked design contract (icon-button h-11/44px, touch target >=44px a11y floor per CLAUDE.md design contract table); correctly labeled as already-locked, not new.

verified.residual_risks:
Two things worth flagging to the owner, neither blocks shipping this as a RATIONALE.md addition:

1. The SEVERITY = mean(...) formula and the 25/75/150% deviation bands are this stream's own invention layered on top of Nielsen's genuinely-T1 three-dimension framework. They are disclosed as such in the verified text (not smuggled in as T1), but they are unproven until the backtest in taste_lab_probe actually runs. If that backtest is skipped, D10 ships as a plausible-looking but uncalibrated rubric, this is a QUESTIONS.md / backtest-task candidate, not a lock-tension, since nothing here touches a frozen LOCKFILE literal.

2. The gate_breach-forces-BLOCKING rule is a genuine formalization of D10's existing two-bucket assertion and does not conflict with any locked value, but it does introduce a new operational commitment (severity-3-plus findings need a mandatory second pass before "ready for review") that touches rule 9's verifier-loop cadence. Confirm the owner wants this as a hard requirement inside the loop rather than a suggestion, since it adds a round to any severity-3/4 finding's path to close.

No myth-screen numbers were used, no frozen literal was reopened, and both named Nielsen sources were confirmed live against nngroup.com to say what the draft claims.
